# For the Animals: An Argument Guide

> The 257 arguments in the catalogue, with the phrase, the main flaw and the address of the answer. Families in order; DIR codes challenge the moral core and IND codes discuss health, the environment, the economy or who defends veganism.

## A. Sentience and moral status (Part DIR)

Do animals count morally?

- [A1. Animals aren't conscious and don't feel pain like we do](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-arent-conscious-and-dont-feel-pain-like-we-do.html): Contradicts the neuroscientific evidence (Cambridge Declaration, 2012; New York Declaration, 2024)
- [A2. Fish and invertebrates don't feel pain](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/fish-and-invertebrates-dont-feel-pain.html): Growing evidence of sentience in fish, cephalopods and decapods
- [A3. Where do you draw the line? Insects? Bacteria?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/where-do-you-draw-the-line-insects-bacteria.html): Continuum fallacy: a fuzzy boundary doesn't erase clear cases
- [A4. Plants feel too](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/plants-feel-too.html): No nervous system and no evidence of experience; and if they did feel, animal farming kills more plants
- [A5. There are different degrees of consciousness, so less conscious animals matter less](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/there-are-different-degrees-of-consciousness-so-less-conscious.html): Minds differ in profile, not in position on a single ruler; applied to humans, the criterion would downgrade babies and people with cognitive disabilities; and a smaller weight still outweighs the taste of a dish
- [A6. Humans suffer more than animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/humans-suffer-more-than-animals.html): Suffering more in some cases doesn't license ignoring those who suffer less; and less cognition often means more suffering and more vulnerability
- [A7. Vegans anthropomorphize animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-anthropomorphize-animals.html): Denying similar mental states is also an error (anthropodenial), and the evidence contradicts it
- [A8. They're just animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/theyre-just-animals.html): Explicit speciesism: species membership as a moral criterion, like race in racism
- [A9. Humans are superior, so we can use the inferior](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/humans-are-superior-so-we-can-use-the-inferior.html): Superior abilities give no right to dominate
- [A10. What matters is the species, not the individual](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-matters-is-the-species-not-the-individual.html): Species don't feel; individuals do
- [A11. Species is biology, race is a social construct](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/species-is-biology-race-is-a-social-construct.html): A biological criterion can be as unjust as a social one: what makes discrimination unjust is giving someone's interests biased weight
- [A12. It's natural to put our own first](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-natural-to-put-our-own-first.html): Partiality lets us prefer our own; it does not let us exploit others
- [A13. I respect animals, but humans come first](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-respect-animals-but-humans-come-first.html): A special status no one explains and that wouldn't pass the veil of ignorance: the weight should depend on the size of the harm, not on species
- [A14. Humans have intrinsic value; animals have instrumental value](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/humans-have-intrinsic-value-animals-have-instrumental-value.html): Circular: it assumes the conclusion
- [A15. Animals aren't rational](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-arent-rational.html): Rationality isn't what makes suffering matter, and the criterion would exclude humans who lack it
- [A16. Animals don't have language](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-dont-have-language.html): An irrelevant criterion for pain; it excludes babies and non-verbal people
- [A17. Animals don't have souls](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-dont-have-souls.html): An unfalsifiable premise used as a public criterion
- [A18. It's normal for humans to be rational](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-normal-for-humans-to-be-rational.html): Treats individuals by what others have, not by what they have
- [A19. Human babies have the potential to be rational](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/human-babies-have-the-potential-to-be-rational.html): Potential doesn't confer the rights of the actual, and it doesn't cover humans without potential
- [A20. Animals don't know they're going to die, so killing them is fine](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-dont-know-theyre-going-to-die-so-killing-them-is-fine.html): What's bad about death is what it takes, not the fear of it: the same reasoning would allow killing babies, people with dementia or people who are asleep
- [A21. Animals aren't persons](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-arent-persons.html): A persuasive definition: pick the concept that excludes them, then conclude they are excluded
- [A22. No duties, no rights](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/no-duties-no-rights.html): Confuses moral agents with moral patients; it would exclude children
- [A23. Rights are a human invention, only for humans](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/rights-are-a-human-invention-only-for-humans.html): Genetic fallacy: where a norm came from doesn't set how far it reaches
- [A24. Morality exists to protect us from each other](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/morality-exists-to-protect-us-from-each-other.html): It would also exclude babies and vulnerable people; and explaining where a practice came from does not justify it
- [A25. Animals are property](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-are-property.html): Describes a legal status; doesn't justify it (as with slavery)

## B. Harm, death and welfare (Part DIR)

Does killing without suffering harm the individual?

- [B1. There is humane slaughter](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/there-is-humane-slaughter.html): A contradiction in terms: there is no compassionate way to kill someone who does not want to die
- [B2. Killing without pain isn't harm](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/killing-without-pain-isnt-harm.html): Death takes away good future experiences; the same holds for humans with no sense of time
- [B3. They had a good life and a quick death](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/they-had-a-good-life-and-a-quick-death.html): A good life doesn't license taking it; the idea is absurd applied to dogs or humans
- [B4. Free-range animals are happy](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/free-range-animals-are-happy.html): They're still killed young; labels have little to do with practice, and changing the scale doesn't change the act
- [B5. Milk and eggs don't kill anyone](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/milk-and-eggs-dont-kill-anyone.html): Male chicks and calves are discarded, and cows and hens are slaughtered when production drops
- [B6. Veal makes use of the calves born in dairy farming](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veal-makes-use-of-the-calves-born-in-dairy-farming.html): The calf isn't born anyway: he's born because the cow must give birth to give milk, and veal makes milk more profitable
- [B7. Without farming, these animals wouldn't even exist](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/without-farming-these-animals-wouldnt-even-exist.html): Bringing someone into existence gives no right to kill them
- [B8. Stressed animals make bad meat, so farmers take good care of them](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/stressed-animals-make-bad-meat-so-farmers-take-good-care-of-them.html): The incentive is small and partial; it doesn't cover suffering that doesn't affect profit
- [B9. Animal scientists take good care of the animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animal-scientists-take-good-care-of-the-animals.html): They care well within the profession's goal, which is production; technical competence doesn't answer whether it is just to raise animals to kill them
- [B10. The law guarantees animal welfare](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-law-guarantees-animal-welfare.html): Laws allow confinement, mutilations without anesthesia and the killing of newborns
- [B11. Live animal transport is regulated and follows standards to ensure the animals' welfare](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/live-animal-transport-is-regulated-and-follows-standards-to-ensure.html): The standards allow very long journeys and are poorly enforced; and even when followed, they regulate the journey of an animal who will be killed at the destination
- [B13. Foie gras is a traditional delicacy, and ducks naturally eat a lot](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/foie-gras-is-a-traditional-delicacy-and-ducks-naturally-eat-a-lot.html): The bird doesn't eat on its own: it's force-fed through a tube until its liver becomes diseased, and European science concluded this harms welfare
- [B14. A lobster boiled alive feels nothing and tastes fresher](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/a-lobster-boiled-alive-feels-nothing-and-tastes-fresher.html): There is serious evidence of pain in crustaceans; the UK recognized them as sentient, and Switzerland requires stunning before killing them
- [B15. Those videos are exceptions or staged](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/those-videos-are-exceptions-or-staged.html): Much of what they show is standard, legal industry practice
- [B16. You don't live on a farm, so you don't know the truth](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/you-dont-live-on-a-farm-so-you-dont-know-the-truth.html): What is criticised is in the industry's own manuals and regulations; and attacking the speaker doesn't show that what is said is wrong

## C. Nature, biology and evolution (Part DIR)

Is what is natural justified?

- [C1. It's natural to eat meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-natural-to-eat-meat.html): Appeal to nature: natural doesn't mean right
- [C2. We have canine teeth; we are omnivores](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/we-have-canine-teeth-we-are-omnivores.html): Being able to eat it isn't needing to; anatomy creates no duty
- [C3. We naturally crave meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/we-naturally-crave-meat.html): A learned and reinforced preference; desire is no justification
- [C4. Eating meat made us evolve](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/eating-meat-made-us-evolve.html): An adaptive past doesn't dictate present morality
- [C5. Lions eat other animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/lions-eat-other-animals.html): Lions aren't moral agents and have no alternative
- [C6. It's the circle of life](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-the-circle-of-life.html): A euphemism: breeding, confining and slaughtering is an industry, not a natural cycle
- [C7. We are animals and part of the ecosystem; no one lives without impact](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/we-are-animals-and-part-of-the-ecosystem-no-one-lives-without-impact.html): Nirvana fallacy and appeal to nature: "harm can't be brought to zero" doesn't mean "it makes no difference how much harm I cause", and "conscious" describes the one who kills, not what happens to the one who dies
- [C8. We're at the top of the food chain](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/were-at-the-top-of-the-food-chain.html): Ecologically false (the average human trophic level is about 2.2) and morally irrelevant
- [C9. Might makes right](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/might-makes-right.html): Social Darwinism: it describes a process, not a norm
- [C10. Farm animals exist for this](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/farm-animals-exist-for-this.html): An imposed purpose: the "function" is assigned by whoever profits
- [C11. Cows need to be milked](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/cows-need-to-be-milked.html): Only because they were made pregnant and bred for overproduction
- [C12. If we don't eat them, animals will take over the planet](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/if-we-dont-eat-them-animals-will-take-over-the-planet.html): Gets the cause backwards: there are so many because they're bred

## D. Tradition, culture and religion (Part DIR)

Does custom justify it?

- [D1. We've always done it](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/weve-always-done-it.html): Appeal to tradition: the same phrase defended slavery and the subjugation of women
- [D2. Everybody eats meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/everybody-eats-meat.html): Appeal to popularity: popular isn't right
- [D3. Barbecues bring the family together](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/barbecues-bring-the-family-together.html): The bond is the gathering, not the animal
- [D4. My grandparents ate meat and lived to 90](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/my-grandparents-ate-meat-and-lived-to-90.html): Anecdotal evidence and survivorship bias
- [D5. I don't want to dishonor my parents and my ancestors](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-dont-want-to-dishonor-my-parents-and-my-ancestors.html): Confuses honoring people with repeating what they did: every generation revises earlier practices, and judging a practice is not condemning those who followed it
- [D6. It's cultural; criticizing it is ethnocentric](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-cultural-criticizing-it-is-ethnocentric.html): Selective cultural relativism: not applied to practices the person condemns
- [D7. Indigenous and traditional peoples eat animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/indigenous-and-traditional-peoples-eat-animals.html): Uses those with no alternative to justify those who have one; veganism already says "as far as is possible and practicable"
- [D8. Great thinkers ate meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/great-thinkers-ate-meat.html): Appeal to authority; many also defended human hierarchies we now reject
- [D9. It's legal; the law allows it](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-legal-the-law-allows-it.html): Legalistic fallacy: the law follows morality, with a delay
- [D10. God gave us dominion over animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/god-gave-us-dominion-over-animals.html): Many traditions read dominion as stewardship; and it is a theological premise, not a public one
- [D11. Jesus ate fish](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/jesus-ate-fish.html): Appeal to authority; a historical context of necessity doesn't carry over
- [D12. My religion approves of eating animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/my-religion-approves-of-eating-animals.html): Permitting is not requiring, and religious traditions themselves forbid unnecessary suffering, which today's production causes on a massive scale
- [D13. Animal sacrifice in religious rituals is freedom of worship](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animal-sacrifice-in-religious-rituals-is-freedom-of-worship.html): Freedom of worship answers whether the state can ban the rite, not whether killing the animal is fair; that question applies equally to the rite and the slaughterhouse, and criticizing only Afro-Brazilian religions is inconsistent
- [D14. I'll pay for my mistakes in my next life](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/ill-pay-for-my-mistakes-in-my-next-life.html): The phrase admits the wrong and postpones the bill, but the animal pays now; the traditions of karma teach non-violence

## E. Relativism, freedom and evasions (Part DIR)

Is it just a matter of choice?

- [E1. It's my personal choice; don't impose your morals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-my-personal-choice-dont-impose-your-morals.html): Personal choice ends where there is a victim; every rule against harm "imposes"
- [E2. The state can't ban what I eat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-state-cant-ban-what-i-eat.html): Switches from "is it wrong?" to "should it be banned?"
- [E3. Morality is relative](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/morality-is-relative.html): Self-refuting and applied selectively; it confuses taste with a claim about harm to others
- [E4. Eating meat isn't an ideology; veganism is](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/eating-meat-isnt-an-ideology-veganism-is.html): The dominant norm is invisible to those who follow it (carnism, Joy 2009)
- [E5. Veganism is opinion, not science](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-opinion-not-science.html): No moral position is "just science", including eating meat
- [E6. Even philosophers don't agree](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/even-philosophers-dont-agree.html): Disagreement isn't a tie; there is strong convergence against factory farming
- [E7. Defending animals is just utilitarianism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/defending-animals-is-just-utilitarianism.html): Equal consideration is a formal principle accepted by rival theories; knocking down utilitarianism doesn't rescue speciesism
- [E8. AIs say that not being vegan isn't wrong](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/ais-say-that-not-being-vegan-isnt-wrong.html): Appeal to authority and, at second hand, to the majority: AI repeats the texts it was trained on and is tuned not to take sides; abstaining is not concluding that it isn't wrong
- [E9. Everything in moderation](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/everything-in-moderation.html): False middle ground: moderation doesn't make an unjustifiable harm acceptable
- [E10. Nobody's perfect; I do what I can](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/nobodys-perfect-i-do-what-i-can.html): True in general, but used to avoid doing what is easy
- [E11. I love animals, but...](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-love-animals-but.html): A contradiction between stated values and practice (the meat paradox)
- [E12. I don't want to see those videos](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-dont-want-to-see-those-videos.html): Willful ignorance: avoiding the information to avoid the obligation
- [E13. He eats meat, but he's a good person](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/he-eats-meat-but-hes-a-good-person.html): Confuses judging the person with judging the act: good people also take part in injustices that custom accepts
- [E14. I admire you, but I can't do it](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-admire-you-but-i-cant-do-it.html): Admiring already means agreeing with the moral point; hard is not impossible, and changing gradually, with support, works
- [E15. I know it's wrong, but I won't change](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-know-its-wrong-but-i-wont-change.html): Admitted weakness of will: concedes the moral point and refuses its consequence

## F. Edge cases and hypotheticals (Part DIR)

What about the desert island?

- [F1. On a desert island, would you eat an animal?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/on-a-desert-island-would-you-eat-an-animal.html): Extreme necessity doesn't justify the practice in normal conditions
- [F2. If a dog and a child were drowning, which would you save?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/if-a-dog-and-a-child-were-drowning-which-would-you-save.html): A preference in a tragic conflict doesn't license exploiting those who aren't in one
- [F3. So should we stop lions from hunting?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/so-should-we-stop-lions-from-hunting.html): Wild animal suffering is a serious question, and it does not favor eating animals
- [F4. What about the insects you kill while driving?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-about-the-insects-you-kill-while-driving.html): Accidental, unavoidable harm differs from intentional, avoidable harm
- [F5. You also kill mosquitoes and rats at home](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/you-also-kill-mosquitoes-and-rats-at-home.html): Self-defense and real conflict differ from breeding animals to eat
- [F6. Killing insects protects us](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/killing-insects-protects-us.html): The danger comes from few species, and the best protection is usually prevention: Brazil's Ministry of Health doesn't recommend poison against scorpions, and the Wolbachia method reduced dengue without killing mosquitoes
- [F7. Oysters and mussels don't feel](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/oysters-and-mussels-dont-feel.html): Partly plausible; it confirms that sentience is the criterion
- [F8. What if they discover that plants feel?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-if-they-discover-that-plants-feel.html): Even in that scenario, eating plants would cause less harm, because animals eat far more plants; not being able to reach zero harm doesn't make everything equivalent
- [F9. What about the eggs from my rescued hen?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-about-the-eggs-from-my-rescued-hen.html): A rare, debatable case with no link to the industry; it doesn't legitimize buying
- [F10. Would you eat an animal that died of natural causes?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/would-you-eat-an-animal-that-died-of-natural-causes.html): No one was killed, so the moral problem is much smaller; but that meat never reaches the market, and refusing to eat a body can be respect, as we do with humans
- [F11. What about meat that gets thrown away?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-about-meat-that-gets-thrown-away.html): Eating without creating demand is a different case; it still reinforces seeing animals as food
- [F12. Would you eat animals if someone paid you well?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/would-you-eat-animals-if-someone-paid-you-well.html): The same dilemma applies to any human cause and never proves it false; refusing on principle is coherent, and so is accepting in order to save far more victims

## G. Health and nutrition (Part IND)

Do we need animal products?

- [G1. Eating animals is necessary to survive](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/eating-animals-is-necessary-to-survive.html): Necessary for whom? Where the alternative exists it is a choice, and the definition of veganism already speaks of doing what is possible and practicable; and the argument concedes the principle that undoes it, since without necessity there is no justification
- [G2. We need animal protein](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/we-need-animal-protein.html): Protein needs are met by legumes, grains and soy
- [G3. Plant protein is incomplete](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/plant-protein-is-incomplete.html): A 1970s myth; variety over the day provides all the essential amino acids
- [G4. If you need B12 supplements, it isn't natural](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/if-you-need-b12-supplements-it-isnt-natural.html): Farm animals also get supplemented B12; and natural is not the criterion (C1)
- [G5. You'll lack iron, zinc and other micronutrients](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/youll-lack-iron-zinc-and-other-micronutrients.html): Plannable with a varied diet; iron deficiency is also common in meat eaters
- [G6. Milk is necessary for your bones](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/milk-is-necessary-for-your-bones.html): Calcium is found in plants and fortified foods
- [G7. Only fish provides omega-3](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/only-fish-provides-omega-3.html): Fish get their DHA from algae, a direct source available to us
- [G8. Plants have antinutrients](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/plants-have-antinutrients.html): Doses and preparation make them irrelevant; populations eating plant-based diets live longer
- [G9. Soy causes female hormones and cancer](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/soy-causes-female-hormones-and-cancer.html): Phytoestrogens aren't estrogen; meta-analyses don't support the myth
- [G10. Children and pregnant women can't be vegan](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/children-and-pregnant-women-cant-be-vegan.html): Major nutrition bodies consider it appropriate at every life stage, with planning
- [G11. Athletes need meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/athletes-need-meat.html): There are elite vegan athletes; adequate protein intake is what matters
- [G12. Vegans are weak, pale and depressed](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-weak-pale-and-depressed.html): A stereotype; the existing correlations have uncertain or reverse causation
- [G13. I know someone who got sick being vegan](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-know-someone-who-got-sick-being-vegan.html): Anecdotal evidence; it confuses a badly planned diet with a vegan diet
- [G14. My body can't adapt](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/my-body-cant-adapt.html): The blood type diet has been refuted; individual complaints are rarely investigated
- [G15. My doctor told me to eat meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/my-doctor-told-me-to-eat-meat.html): An appeal to individual authority against institutional positions
- [G16. A carnivore, paleo or keto diet is healthiest](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/a-carnivore-paleo-or-keto-diet-is-healthiest.html): Weak, short-term evidence that contradicts the large cohort studies
- [G17. The WHO exaggerates; red meat isn't bad for you](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-who-exaggerates-red-meat-isnt-bad-for-you.html): Cherry picking against the consensus (IARC: processed meat Group 1, red meat Group 2A)
- [G18. Ultra-processed vegan foods are worse than meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/ultra-processed-vegan-foods-are-worse-than-meat.html): False dichotomy: veganism doesn't require ultra-processed foods
- [G19. Fruitarianism isn't healthy, so veganism isn't either](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/fruitarianism-isnt-healthy-so-veganism-isnt-either.html): Veganism isn't fruitarianism: an all-fruit diet is risky, but a varied, planned vegan diet with B12 is considered adequate
- [G20. Veganism is an eating disorder in disguise](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-an-eating-disorder-in-disguise.html): The association exists, but the disorder usually comes before the diet; community vegans show no more signs of disorder, and the cause of a tragedy is the illness

## H. Environment, ecology and agriculture (Part IND)

Is veganism worse for the planet?

- [H1. Vegans' soy is destroying the Amazon](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-soy-is-destroying-the-amazon.html): Most soy becomes animal feed; pasture is the main driver of deforestation
- [H2. Harvests kill animals; vegans kill too](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/harvests-kill-animals-vegans-kill-too.html): Animal farming uses far more cropland (for feed) and land
- [H3. Plant monoculture destroys as much as industrial animal farming](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/plant-monoculture-destroys-as-much-as-industrial-animal-farming.html): Most soy and much of the grain feed farmed animals; eating plants reduces agricultural land, and comparing the worst cropland with the best animal farming is unfair
- [H4. Avocados and almonds use a lot of water](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/avocados-and-almonds-use-a-lot-of-water.html): A selective comparison; per nutrient, animal products lead in water and land use
- [H5. Imported vegan food pollutes in transport](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/imported-vegan-food-pollutes-in-transport.html): Transport is a small share of emissions; what you eat matters more than how far it traveled
- [H6. Livestock pollutes little; the problem is fossil fuels](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/livestock-pollutes-little-the-problem-is-fossil-fuels.html): False dichotomy; food systems account for about a third of emissions
- [H7. Cow methane is biogenic; it doesn't count](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/cow-methane-is-biogenic-it-doesnt-count.html): Methane has a strong short-term effect; growing herds increase warming
- [H8. Regenerative grazing sequesters carbon](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/regenerative-grazing-sequesters-carbon.html): Limited, temporary sequestration that cannot scale; it needs more land per calorie
- [H9. Cattle graze where crops can't grow](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/cattle-graze-where-crops-cant-grow.html): Partly true, but that land could be rewilded and produces few calories
- [H10. Cattle prevent wildfires; they're firefighter cattle](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/cattle-prevent-wildfires-theyre-firefighter-cattle.html): The effect is local and disputed; ranching also causes deforestation and burning, and fire can be managed without raising animals
- [H11. Agriculture can't work without manure](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/agriculture-cant-work-without-manure.html): Green manures and compost exist; the manure comes from crops grown for feed
- [H12. Local, organic meat is sustainable](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/local-organic-meat-is-sustainable.html): Grass-fed beef usually needs more land and emits as much or more per kilo
- [H13. What matters is how food is grown, not whether it comes from animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-matters-is-how-food-is-grown-not-whether-it-comes-from-animals.html): False dichotomy: you can choose plants and care about how they are grown; the type of food weighs more than the production method, and none of it answers what happens to the animal
- [H14. If meat is sustainable, there's no problem](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/if-meat-is-sustainable-theres-no-problem.html): Reduces a moral question about victims to an environmental one
- [H15. Leather and wool are more sustainable than synthetics, which are plastic](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/leather-and-wool-are-more-sustainable-than-synthetics-which-are.html): Leather and wool also have a high impact, the numbers are disputed, and the choice isn't only between animal and plastic
- [H16. Sustainable fishing and aquaculture solve it](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sustainable-fishing-and-aquaculture-solve-it.html): Bycatch, overfishing and feed made from wild fish; the suffering continues
- [H17. Eating insects is the sustainable protein of the future](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/eating-insects-is-the-sustainable-protein-of-the-future.html): Trades environmental impact for trillions of probable victims; plant proteins are just as efficient, with no one to suffer
- [H18. Hunting controls populations](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/hunting-controls-populations.html): It often causes the imbalance it claims to fix; non-lethal methods exist
- [H19. Kangaroo meat is the most sustainable meat there is](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/kangaroo-meat-is-the-most-sustainable-meat-there-is.html): It has a lower impact than beef, but comes from shooting at scale, with joeys killed; plant foods have an even lower impact

## I. Other uses: testing, clothing, entertainment, work and companionship (Part IND)

And beyond the plate?

- [I1. Animal testing has saved millions of lives](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animal-testing-has-saved-millions-of-lives.html): A benefit doesn't justify using those who can't consent; translational failure rates are high
- [I2. If you take medicine, you can't oppose testing](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/if-you-take-medicine-you-cant-oppose-testing.html): Tu quoque; testing is required by law, not chosen by the patient
- [I3. Cosmetics tested on animals are safer](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/cosmetics-tested-on-animals-are-safer.html): Cosmetics aren't medicine; the EU has banned it since 2013 and Brazil restricts it since 2023, and safety is ensured with known ingredients and animal-free methods
- [I4. Medical and veterinary students need to practice on animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/medical-and-veterinary-students-need-to-practice-on-animals.html): Systematic reviews show that harm-free methods teach as well or better; living tissue can be practiced on without killing healthy animals
- [I5. Pig organs will save thousands of lives](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/pig-organs-will-save-thousands-of-lives.html): The organ shortage is real, but there are paths that do not breed animals for their organs: human donation, artificial and grown organs
- [I6. Traditional medicine has used animal parts for millennia](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/traditional-medicine-has-used-animal-parts-for-millennia.html): Being old does not prove efficacy; bears are caged for years for bile, and the useful compound is already synthesized
- [I7. Leather is just a byproduct of meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/leather-is-just-a-byproduct-of-meat.html): Profitable byproducts subsidize slaughter
- [I8. A fur coat is natural and comes from regulated farms](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/a-fur-coat-is-natural-and-comes-from-regulated-farms.html): The animals live in wire cages, fur has a high environmental impact, and several countries have banned the farms
- [I9. Sheep need to be shorn](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sheep-need-to-be-shorn.html): Only because they were bred for excessive wool; mulesing, and slaughter when production ends
- [I10. Silk and down are natural and don't harm animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/silk-and-down-are-natural-and-dont-harm-animals.html): In conventional silk the silkworm is boiled in its cocoon, and plucking feathers from live birds causes pain, according to EFSA
- [I11. Bees make extra honey](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/bees-make-extra-honey.html): Honey is the bees' food reserve; honeybees compete with native pollinators
- [I12. Zoos conserve species and educate](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/zoos-conserve-species-and-educate.html): Few of the species kept are endangered or reintroduced
- [I13. Aquariums and dolphin parks are harmless](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/aquariums-and-dolphin-parks-are-harmless.html): Severe captivity for wide-ranging animals with complex social lives
- [I14. Wildlife sanctuaries protect animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/wildlife-sanctuaries-protect-animals.html): The name is not regulated: many "sanctuaries" are zoos that breed, sell and display animals; real ones rescue, don't breed and don't let the public handle them
- [I15. Safaris and animal tours are harmless tourism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/safaris-and-animal-tours-are-harmless-tourism.html): Watching free animals from a distance is not the same as riding, holding or swimming with captive ones; in an Oxford study, 18 of 24 types of attraction harmed welfare
- [I16. Rodeos, bullfights and circuses are culture](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/rodeos-bullfights-and-circuses-are-culture.html): Appeal to tradition (D1) applied to suffering imposed for entertainment
- [I17. A rodeo animal is a well-treated athlete and only bucks for a few seconds](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/a-rodeo-animal-is-a-well-treated-athlete-and-only-bucks-for-a-few.html): The animal bucks because the flank strap and spurs provoke it, doesn't choose to compete, and the rodeo law itself recognizes the risk of cruelty
- [I18. The fighting bull lives free in the field and dies fighting](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-fighting-bull-lives-free-in-the-field-and-dies-fighting.html): A good life doesn't justify a slow death as a spectacle, the fight isn't fair because the bull is weakened first, and preserving the breed benefits no bull
- [I19. Circus animals are well treated and part of the family](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/circus-animals-are-well-treated-and-part-of-the-family.html): A bond isn't welfare; traveling life doesn't meet these animals' needs, and more than 40 countries restrict it
- [I20. Animals in films, ads and videos are trained, well-cared-for actors](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/animals-in-films-ads-and-videos-are-trained-well-cared-for-actors.html): The credit has documented failures, videos of exotic animals encourage the trade, and digital effects replace the use
- [I21. Horses like working and being ridden](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/horses-like-working-and-being-ridden.html): A convenient projection by those who benefit
- [I22. Racehorses and sporting dogs live better than many people](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/racehorses-and-sporting-dogs-live-better-than-many-people.html): The care lasts while the animal earns, racing kills and discards, and human poverty is an injustice to fix, not a yardstick for using animals
- [I23. In sport fishing the fish is released](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/in-sport-fishing-the-fish-is-released.html): Injury, stress and post-release mortality; pain as a pastime
- [I24. I fish what I eat; it's more honest than buying at the store](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-fish-what-i-eat-its-more-honest-than-buying-at-the-store.html): Being honest about a harm doesn't make it necessary; a fish out of water dies by asphyxia, with minutes of pain
- [I25. Trophy hunting funds conservation](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/trophy-hunting-funds-conservation.html): Little money reaches conservation; it uses individuals as tools
- [I26. The cart is the carter's livelihood, and the horse is well cared for](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-cart-is-the-carters-livelihood-and-the-horse-is-well-cared-for.html): The worker's income is real; the way forward is to replace the horse with a vehicle, with support, not to keep the animal on the asphalt
- [I27. Guide and assistance dogs are well cared for and do important work](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/guide-and-assistance-dogs-are-well-cared-for-and-do-important-work.html): It's a borderline case, discussed with nuance; a hard case doesn't make the easy ones acceptable, such as breeding for slaughter
- [I28. Police and detection dogs are well cared for and save lives](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/police-and-detection-dogs-are-well-cared-for-and-save-lives.html): The dog is put at risk without being able to choose, and the care depends on usefulness; a use that saves lives doesn't justify those that don't
- [I29. Buying a pedigree dog or cat doesn't hurt anyone](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/buying-a-pedigree-dog-or-cat-doesnt-hurt-anyone.html): Commercial breeding uses breeding females, shapes breeds with health problems and competes with shelter adoption
- [I30. The bird was born in a cage; it wouldn't survive if released](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-bird-was-born-in-a-cage-it-wouldnt-survive-if-released.html): That calls for caring well for the bird that exists, not buying or breeding others to live caged; the market feeds trafficking
- [I31. Having a pet is exploitation too, and your cat eats meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/having-a-pet-is-exploitation-too-and-your-cat-eats-meat.html): Adopting and caring differs from breeding to use; cats need nutrients, not meat; and none of this licenses eating animals
- [I32. A shock collar is just a stimulus; it doesn't hurt the dog](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/a-shock-collar-is-just-a-stimulus-it-doesnt-hurt-the-dog.html): It works because it's unpleasant, doesn't treat the cause of barking, and reward-based training works as well or better

## J. Practicality, economy and society (Part IND)

Is it feasible and fair to ask this?

- [J1. Veganism is expensive](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-expensive.html): Beans, rice, grains and vegetables are among the cheapest foods
- [J2. Poor people have no access](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/poor-people-have-no-access.html): A real barrier for some, which doesn't apply to the person objecting; and many cultures have old vegetarian traditions
- [J3. It's hard; I don't have time](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-hard-i-dont-have-time.html): Initial difficulty isn't impossibility; inconvenience doesn't justify harm
- [J4. Eating out, traveling and parties become impossible](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/eating-out-traveling-and-parties-become-impossible.html): Exaggerates the social cost; options keep growing and adapting is quick
- [J5. Meat tastes good](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/meat-tastes-good.html): Taste as a justification for killing: no other context accepts this
- [J6. Vegan food is bland](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegan-food-is-bland.html): A generalization from unfamiliarity; most spices and many dishes are already plant-based
- [J7. I eat little meat; that's enough](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-eat-little-meat-thats-enough.html): Reducing is better than nothing, but it doesn't justify what is left
- [J8. I don't want to feel left out; eating together is how you belong](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-dont-want-to-feel-left-out-eating-together-is-how-you-belong.html): Belonging doesn't require eating the same dish, and the social discomfort of refusing doesn't compare with the cost to the animal
- [J9. Agriculture is the backbone of the economy](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/agriculture-is-the-backbone-of-the-economy.html): Economic importance is not a moral justification; it ignores subsidies and external costs
- [J10. Vegans are against farmers](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-against-farmers.html): Treats farming as a single block: veganism opposes breeding and killing animals, not crop growing, which is where vegan food comes from
- [J11. Farmers and slaughterhouse workers would lose their jobs](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/farmers-and-slaughterhouse-workers-would-lose-their-jobs.html): An argument used against every moral reform; transitions can be planned
- [J12. This is my living; it feeds my family](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/this-is-my-living-it-feeds-my-family.html): Economic dependence explains why change is hard, but it does not make the activity just; the way out is a planned, supported transition
- [J13. Fishers and ranchers would lose their identity](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/fishers-and-ranchers-would-lose-their-identity.html): Identity doesn't justify harm to others; it calls for a just transition
- [J14. Billions of people depend on fish for protein](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/billions-of-people-depend-on-fish-for-protein.html): The FAO figure refers to 20% of animal protein, not of protein needs, and the dependence of some doesn't justify consumption by those who have a choice
- [J15. Veganism has become big business](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-has-become-big-business.html): Genetic fallacy: a moral position doesn't become false because someone profits from it, and the business of exploiting animals is far bigger
- [J16. There are more important human problems](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/there-are-more-important-human-problems.html): Priority fallacy: eating plants doesn't take time from any other cause
- [J17. People are dying in a war and you're worried about animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/people-are-dying-in-a-war-and-youre-worried-about-animals.html): The animals are victims of the same war; the cost of helping them is far smaller than the sentence assumes, and a cost existing decides nothing, since that holds for every use of resources
- [J18. Veganism is a political ideology or a globalist agenda](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-a-political-ideology-or-a-globalist-agenda.html): Guilt by association and conspiracy theory; it doesn't assess the argument
- [J19. What would we do with the animals if everyone went vegan?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/what-would-we-do-with-the-animals-if-everyone-went-vegan.html): A gradual change reduces births; the problem is created by breeding itself
- [J20. A vegan world is utopian](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/a-vegan-world-is-utopian.html): Confuses full, immediate feasibility with a present individual duty

## K. Effectiveness and individual responsibility (Part IND)

Does my choice change anything?

- [K1. One person doesn't make a difference](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/one-person-doesnt-make-a-difference.html): Expected-value reasoning: the elasticity is below 1 but positive, and buying less leads to producing less
- [K2. The animal is already dead](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-animal-is-already-dead.html): The purchase pays for restocking, that is, the next death
- [K3. I don't kill; I just eat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-dont-kill-i-just-eat.html): Outsourced morality: paying for the act is taking part in it
- [K4. The problem is the industry, not consumers](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-problem-is-the-industry-not-consumers.html): The industry exists to meet demand: system and consumer sustain each other
- [K5. There is no ethical consumption under capitalism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/there-is-no-ethical-consumption-under-capitalism.html): A partial truth used to erase huge differences in harm
- [K6. Vegans should fight for laws, not diets](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-should-fight-for-laws-not-diets.html): False dichotomy; personal consistency and political action complement each other
- [K7. Vegans shouldn't get into politics, because politics is dirty](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-shouldnt-get-into-politics-because-politics-is-dirty.html): Staying out doesn't keep decisions clean, it leaves them to whoever is already there; the gains for animals came from politics, and the risk of corruption calls for care, not absence
- [K8. Radical veganism pushes people away](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/radical-veganism-pushes-people-away.html): May be a fair point about strategy, but it is neither a moral rebuttal nor a personal excuse
- [K9. Vegans will always be a minority](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-will-always-be-a-minority.html): Being a minority doesn't make something wrong or useless: change begins with a few, each person reduces demand, and animal protection laws change without a vegan majority
- [K10. I'll wait for cultivated meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/ill-wait-for-cultivated-meat.html): Postpones the duty until it costs nothing

## L. Attacks on veganism and vegans (Part IND)

Can the people saying this be trusted?

- [L1. Vegans are annoying and think they are better](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-annoying-and-think-they-are-better.html): Ad hominem: the messenger's behavior doesn't change whether the message is valid
- [L2. Vegans are all hippies](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-all-hippies.html): A stereotype and an attack on the person: animals' suffering doesn't depend on the lifestyle of whoever points it out
- [L3. Vegans are crazy; they have mental problems](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-crazy-they-have-mental-problems.html): An attack on the person: the asker's health doesn't change the answer, the link with depression doesn't show cause, and using mental disorders as insults reinforces stigma
- [L4. Sentientists are even crazier than vegans](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sentientists-are-even-crazier-than-vegans.html): Attack on the person and appeal to ridicule: strangeness is not error, and the fair test is to apply the same scenario to humans and examine the premise
- [L5. Vegan activists are radicals and extremists](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegan-activists-are-radicals-and-extremists.html): Judging a cause by the methods of a minority
- [L6. Meat is for real men](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/meat-is-for-real-men.html): A gender stereotype; masculinity is neither a moral nor a nutritional criterion
- [L7. Veganism is a cult, a religion](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-a-cult-a-religion.html): A label used to avoid evaluating; veganism rests on public arguments
- [L8. Veganism is moral puritanism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-moral-puritanism.html): A label in place of a rebuttal: veganism is about harm to third parties, not the purity of the eater, and every morality goes against natural impulses
- [L9. Hitler was a vegetarian](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/hitler-was-a-vegetarian.html): Reductio ad Hitlerum and guilt by association; historically doubtful
- [L10. Raising vegan children is imposing an ideology](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/raising-vegan-children-is-imposing-an-ideology.html): Every family passes values on to its children, and serving meat is also the parents' choice; what matters is caring for the child's health and explaining the reasons
- [L11. You use a phone, so you're a hypocrite](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/you-use-a-phone-so-youre-a-hypocrite.html): Tu quoque: someone's inconsistency doesn't make what they say false
- [L12. Veganism isn't 100% cruelty-free](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-isnt-100-cruelty-free.html): Nirvana fallacy: reducing harm doesn't require eliminating it entirely
- [L13. Vegans shouldn't use artificial intelligence](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-shouldnt-use-artificial-intelligence.html): Veganism doesn't promise zero impact, only not to exploit animals; AI's cost is real, but diet weighs far more, and 'it isn't natural' settles nothing
- [L14. Vegans shouldn't watch violent films or play violent games](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-shouldnt-watch-violent-films-or-play-violent-games.html): Depicting violence isn't committing it, and fiction has no victims; when an animal was really harmed on set, the criticism is fair and avoiding the work is consistent
- [L15. Vegans are speciesists too](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-speciesists-too.html): Tu quoque: having a bias doesn't license harming anyone, it calls for correction; and speciesism is the unjustified disregard of interests, not any preference
- [L16. You don't feel empathy for every animal in the world either](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/you-dont-feel-empathy-for-every-animal-in-the-world-either.html): The question isn't empathy: it is limited and biased, and where it fails we use reason and principles, as we do with distant humans
- [L17. If vegans eat fake meat, they want meat](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/if-vegans-eat-fake-meat-they-want-meat.html): The problem was never the taste; it was the victim
- [L18. There are sexist, racist and transphobic vegans](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/there-are-sexist-racist-and-transphobic-vegans.html): Tu quoque and an attack on the messenger: a vegan's failing in another cause doesn't change what happens to animals, and the same reasoning would bring down any cause
- [L19. Vegans defend animals, but they support abortion](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-defend-animals-but-they-support-abortion.html): Tu quoque and generalization: veganism has no position on abortion, the two cases have different structures, and someone's inconsistency wouldn't justify exploiting animals
- [L20. Vegans care more about animals than people](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-care-more-about-animals-than-people.html): False dilemma and generalization; empathy is not a zero-sum resource
- [L21. Comparing animal farming to slavery or the Holocaust is offensive](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/comparing-animal-farming-to-slavery-or-the-holocaust-is-offensive.html): Distinguish structural analogy from moral equivalence; handle with care and sources
- [L22. Vegans are racist, because they criticize Afro-Brazilian religions](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-racist-because-they-criticize-afro-brazilian-religions.html): Generalizes the selective criticism of some: the consistent criterion criticizes every avoidable killing of animals, starts with the industry and doesn't pick a people as its target
- [L23. Vegans are against religion](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-against-religion.html): False generalization: there are vegans in every religion, whole traditions teach not harming animals, and veganism is compatible with faith and with the absence of faith
- [L24. Veganism is just a fad diet](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/veganism-is-just-a-fad-diet.html): Confuses an ethical position about not harming animals with a menu chosen for health or looks
- [L25. Vegans support pseudoscience](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-support-pseudoscience.html): Some vegans spread pseudoscience, but the case for animals rests on sentience and the nutritional consensus; judging an idea by its worst advocates would bring down any cause
- [L26. Vegan documentaries are manipulated](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegan-documentaries-are-manipulated.html): Generalizes from some films' errors to everything: the footage shows standard, legal practices, and the moral conclusion doesn't depend on any film
- [L27. Most vegans give up](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/most-vegans-give-up.html): Difficulty sticking to it says nothing about whether it is right
- [L28. Vegans treat vegetarians as enemies](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-treat-vegetarians-as-enemies.html): An attack on the messenger: some vegans' hostility is a mistake, but the criticism is of milk and egg production, not of people
- [L29. Vegans think they're the only ones who really defend animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-think-theyre-the-only-ones-who-really-defend-animals.html): Generalizes from some vegans and confuses criticizing an inconsistency with despising people; those who rescue animals already accept that animals matter
- [L30. I'll eat double to make up for you](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/ill-eat-double-to-make-up-for-you.html): An emotional reaction (reactance), not an argument
- [L31. My food beats yours](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/my-food-beats-yours.html): A taunt, not an argument: the pleasure of taste doesn't weigh against someone's life, and much vegan food is the same food as always
- [L32. Look what you're missing](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/look-what-youre-missing.html): Showing the plate doesn't answer the question about who became the plate; temptation doesn't make the act just

## M. Ex-vegans: why I gave up (Part IND)

Does having given up change what is right?

- [M1. I stopped being vegan because I started feeling unwell](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-stopped-being-vegan-because-i-started-feeling-unwell.html): The discomfort is real but rarely investigated: it usually comes from eating too little, lack of B12 or poor planning, and can be solved without animal products
- [M2. I was vegan for my health, and I changed my mind](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-was-vegan-for-my-health-and-i-changed-my-mind.html): Changing your mind about health does not answer the reason concerning animals, which may have existed and lost strength, or never been examined
- [M3. Being vegan limited me when eating at my relatives' homes](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/being-vegan-limited-me-when-eating-at-my-relatives-homes.html): The social cost is real, but there are ways through: talking beforehand, bringing a dish to share, eating what is already vegan on the table
- [M4. Being vegan is hard if you travel a lot](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/being-vegan-is-hard-if-you-travel-a-lot.html): The difficulty of some meals justifies, at most, a genuine exception, not giving up veganism at home
- [M5. I stopped being vegan because I'm at a different stage of life](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-stopped-being-vegan-because-im-at-a-different-stage-of-life.html): A stage of life changes what is easy, not what happens to the animals; a hard stage calls for adjustments, not for giving up
- [M6. Vegans are annoying and bossy; I don't want to be part of that group](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/vegans-are-annoying-and-bossy-i-dont-want-to-be-part-of-that-group.html): Confuses the principle with the group: you can leave hostile people without ceasing to spare animals
- [M7. I don't want to be labeled; the label brings pressure](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-dont-want-to-be-labeled-the-label-brings-pressure.html): Confuses the label with the practice: the name is optional, and what reaches the animals is what one does
- [M8. It became an obsession; I lived with guilt](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/it-became-an-obsession-i-lived-with-guilt.html): False dichotomy between total purity and giving up: veganism asks for what is possible and practicable, not perfection
- [M9. I was vegan and started getting too radical, too rigid](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-was-vegan-and-started-getting-too-radical-too-rigid.html): The rigidity comes from how veganism is lived, not from the principle; the way can change without giving up the reason concerning animals
- [M10. I used to be vegan; I know what I'm talking about](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/i-used-to-be-vegan-i-know-what-im-talking-about.html): Having been vegan gives experience of how it was for that person, not authority on the moral question

## N. Wild animals, new minds and the future (Part DIR)

Should we help, not just stop harming?

- [N1. Wild animals live free and happy](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/wild-animals-live-free-and-happy.html): The adults we see are the exception: in most species, almost all young die shortly after birth, from hunger, cold, disease or predation
- [N2. Suffering and death are part of nature](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/suffering-and-death-are-part-of-nature.html): Diseases are part of human life too, and that was never a reason not to treat them; the harm isn't smaller for the victim because no one is to blame
- [N3. A balanced nature is good for animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/a-balanced-nature-is-good-for-animals.html): Balance measures numbers, not wellbeing; and environmental programmes kill thousands of animals for goals we would never accept for humans
- [N4. We didn't cause it, so we have no duty to help](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/we-didnt-cause-it-so-we-have-no-duty-to-help.html): Omission bias: no one would accept this reasoning about a drowning child or flood victims
- [N5. Who are we to interfere with nature?](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/who-are-we-to-interfere-with-nature.html): We interfere all the time, with cities, farming and medicine; and no one calls helping an injured person arrogant
- [N6. Meddling with nature is wrong; we could make everything worse](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/meddling-with-nature-is-wrong-we-could-make-everything-worse.html): Risk calls for study and caution, as in medicine, not for omission: that is the proposal of welfare biology
- [N7. It's impossible to solve suffering in nature; it's too big and complex](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/its-impossible-to-solve-suffering-in-nature-its-too-big-and-complex.html): Not being able to solve everything is no reason to do nothing: we already vaccinate foxes, rescue animals in disasters, and can research to do more
- [N8. Using medicine and genetics to end suffering is playing God](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/using-medicine-and-genetics-to-end-suffering-is-playing-god.html): We already use anaesthesia, vaccines and painkillers without calling it playing God; the issue is safety and consent, not the natural origin of pain
- [N9. Helping wild animals isn't veganism; it's a different cause](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/helping-wild-animals-isnt-veganism-its-a-different-cause.html): If sentience is what matters, suffering doesn't stop counting because we didn't cause it; and one cause doesn't stop us researching the other
- [N10. Sentientists are against preserving species and biodiversity](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sentientists-are-against-preserving-species-and-biodiversity.html): Species and biodiversity don't feel: the sentientist supports preservation when it is good for individuals and questions it only when it harms them
- [N11. Sentientists want to get rid of forests](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sentientists-want-to-get-rid-of-forests.html): Straw man: the real proposals are research, targeted help and caution, and recognizing that there is suffering in a place isn't proposing to destroy it
- [N12. Sentientists want to get rid of predators](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sentientists-want-to-get-rid-of-predators.html): Killing predators is what the position rejects, for the very ecological reason the objection gives; what exists is long-term research on reducing predation without causing harm
- [N13. Sentientists defend parasitism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sentientists-defend-parasitism.html): Incomplete count: without treatment many parasites die with the host, death is only a harm to those who feel and would have a good life, and preventing is not killing
- [N14. Sentientists support population control and antinatalism for wild animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sentientists-support-population-control-and-antinatalism-for-wild.html): It's partly true, but there's no ready-made answer: it depends on which animals would be harmed and which would benefit, and the serious position is to research before acting
- [N15. Sentientists give the same weight to insects, invertebrates and mammals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/sentientists-give-the-same-weight-to-insects-invertebrates-and-mammals.html): Confuses equal consideration with equal weight: similar interests weigh the same, and each being's weight depends on how much it can feel, which is uncertain but not zero
- [N16. Machines will never feel; robots and AIs need no rights](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/machines-will-never-feel-robots-and-ais-need-no-rights.html): If an artificial mind ever feels, its substrate matters no more than species does; and uncertainty calls for precaution before creating minds at scale
- [N17. Those not yet born don't matter](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/those-not-yet-born-dont-matter.html): Whoever is born will feel what we leave them: that's why burying toxic waste is wrong, even if the victims don't exist yet
- [N18. We have to worry about future humans, not about animals](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/we-have-to-worry-about-future-humans-not-about-animals.html): It has already accepted the hard part, that future beings count; what is missing is why, once that future arrives, only the humans in it would count, and most of those who will feel will not be human
- [N19. There's no way to plan for the long term, since we can't predict a distant future](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/theres-no-way-to-plan-for-the-long-term-since-we-cant-predict-a.html): It works against plans that depend on getting one scenario right, not against actions that pay off in almost all of them; and uncertainty cuts both ways
- [N20. The future will certainly be better, so there's no need to worry so much](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/the-future-will-certainly-be-better-so-theres-no-need-to-worry-so-much.html): Moral progress is not automatic: every advance had someone making it happen; and with animals the recent trend runs the other way, because power grew without consideration keeping up
- [N21. That's science fiction; we have real problems now](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/arguments/thats-science-fiction-we-have-real-problems-now.html): An uncertain but immense risk can deserve attention, and much of what reduces future suffering, like widening the moral circle, also helps now

## Stop saying this

- [V1. Going vegan will make you healthier.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/going-vegan-will-make-you-healthier.html): It's imprecise: any badly planned diet carries risks.
- [V2. Veganism would end world hunger.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/veganism-would-end-world-hunger.html): It ignores that hunger is largely a problem of distribution and political will, not just of farm output.
- [V3. Go vegan for the planet.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/go-vegan-for-the-planet.html): The problem isn't that the environmental argument is false. It's that it is fragile exactly where it most needs to be solid: if the reason to reject animal farming is its environmental impact, cleaner animal farming would solve the problem without solving anything for the animals.
- [V4. Meat eaters are psychopaths.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/meat-eaters-are-psychopaths.html): It's inaccurate and counterproductive. Most of these people have genuine emotional bonds.
- [V5. Non-vegans are our enemies, and hating them is normal.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/non-vegans-are-our-enemies-and-hating-them-is-normal.html): Almost every vegan was once a non-vegan. People who eat animals today are, in general, where we used to be: repeating a habit learned in childhood, without ever having stopped to examine it. Treating them as enemies is treating who we were as an enemy.
- [V6. There's no such thing as an ex-vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/theres-no-such-thing-as-an-ex-vegan.html): Being vegan is an ethical position held up by arguments and repeated choices, not a genetic trait. Any such position can be abandoned. There are ex-abolitionists, ex-feminists and ex-pacifists for the same reason.
- [V7. Using force to protect animals is always wrong.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/using-force-to-protect-animals-is-always-wrong.html): The question is more open than that certainty suggests. Absolute pacifism trips over its own logic: refusing to stop a greater harm, in practice, lets it happen. And we accept forceful intervention for humans who cannot defend themselves, such as a child being attacked.
- [V8. Every vegan has to be friendly with non-vegans, or we won't convince anyone.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/every-vegan-has-to-be-friendly-with-non-vegans-or-we-wont-convince.html): There is a lot of truth here: hostile conversations tend to produce defensiveness and rejection, and someone who feels attacked stops listening. Treating the person with respect helps.
- [V9. We have to confront non-vegans, since they're the extremists.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/we-have-to-confront-non-vegans-since-theyre-the-extremists.html): Part of the sentence has a basis: confronting an unjust practice is legitimate, and thinking it wrong to kill animals needlessly is not an extreme position.
- [V10. Being vegan is very expensive.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/being-vegan-is-very-expensive.html): Coming from a vegan, the phrase confirms one of the myths most used against veganism, and pushes away people who might join.
- [V11. Each vegan saves 200 animals a year.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/each-vegan-saves-200-animals-a-year.html): The number looks precise, but it's a simple division: total animals killed divided by the number of people. It ignores that production doesn't fall in the same proportion as demand, because prices drop and others buy part of what was not bought.
- [V12. All animals are slaughtered fully conscious, without stunning.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/all-animals-are-slaughtered-fully-conscious-without-stunning.html): It's a generalization. In the European Union and in Brazil, the law requires stunning cattle, pigs and poultry before bleeding, and in the United States federal law requires it for mammals, though not for poultry. Most slaughter follows these rules, even with failures and exceptions.
- [V13. In India almost everyone is vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/in-india-almost-everyone-is-vegan.html): It confuses vegetarianism with veganism. About 39% of Indian adults say they are vegetarian, and milk consumption in the country is very high.
- [V14. Hitler wasn't even really a vegetarian.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/hitler-wasnt-even-really-a-vegetarian.html): Hitler's diet is debated by historians, and answering on historical grounds unintentionally accepts that it would matter to the discussion.
- [V15. Jesus was a vegetarian.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/jesus-was-a-vegetarian.html): The Gospels describe Jesus eating and offering fish, and the theories that he was vegetarian, for example through a link with the Essenes, have no solid historical basis.
- [V16. Great geniuses like Einstein and Da Vinci were vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/great-geniuses-like-einstein-and-da-vinci-were-vegan.html): It's the same appeal to authority as the opposing argument, just from the other side. If the diet of famous thinkers doesn't prove that eating meat is right, it doesn't prove that not eating it is either.
- [V17. We should love animals.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/we-should-love-animals.html): It confuses affection with respect. No one is obliged to love humans or animals, but no one has the right to harm them for that reason.
- [V18. I'm vegan out of compassion for all living beings.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/im-vegan-out-of-compassion-for-all-living-beings.html): Veganism's criterion isn't being alive, it's being sentient. Plants, fungi and single-celled organisms are alive, but there's no evidence they can be harmed in the sense that matters.
- [V19. God didn't make animals for humans.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/god-didnt-make-animals-for-humans.html): Religious arguments of this kind depend on belief, not on reasons anyone can share, so they don't persuade people of a different faith.
- [V20. Pigs are smarter than a three-year-old child.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/pigs-are-smarter-than-a-three-year-old-child.html): The comparison is widely shared but rests on weak studies. The experiment in which pigs used a mirror to find food has not been replicated, and comparing the intelligence of species by a single measure has no solid basis.
- [V21. Humans come first.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/humans-come-first.html): As a general principle, it is plain speciesism, whether applied by vegans or non-vegans.
- [V22. Comparing it to slavery pushes people away.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/comparing-it-to-slavery-pushes-people-away.html): It can look like a strategic concern. The test is simple: if it were shown that the comparison is more effective at improving the situation of animals, would you start supporting it? If the answer is no, the objection was always moral, just dressed up as tactics.
- [V23. Don't show the footage; it's too shocking.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/dont-show-the-footage-its-too-shocking.html): At some point this caution becomes an inverted priority: it treats the discomfort of the viewer as more important than the suffering of those being filmed.
- [V24. This partial law is unfair to the other animals.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/this-partial-law-is-unfair-to-the-other-animals.html): It sounds like an even stronger commitment, but it proves too much: since it's impossible to ban every form of exploitation at once, someone who cares about outcomes would prefer a real reduction in suffering to none.
- [V25. Not your mom, not your milk.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/not-your-mom-not-your-milk.html): It's an appeal to nature: it suggests milk from another species is wrong because nature didn't reserve it for us. Natural doesn't define right, and vegans point out this same mistake in "it's natural to eat meat".
- [V26. No adult animal drinks milk.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/no-adult-animal-drinks-milk.html): It's an appeal to nature. We do many things no other animal does, like cooking, and that doesn't make them wrong; other animals not drinking milk doesn't make milk wrong either.
- [V27. Eggs are chicken periods.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/eggs-are-chicken-periods.html): Even if the comparison were accurate, it says nothing moral. Being gross doesn't make something wrong, and not being gross wouldn't make it right. The listener can simply say they don't care.
- [V28. Meat eaters eat more soy than vegans.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/meat-eaters-eat-more-soy-than-vegans.html): It's true that about three quarters of the world's soy becomes animal feed, and that is a good argument about deforestation.
- [V29. In a room with a rabbit and an apple, a child eats the apple and plays with the rabbit.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/in-a-room-with-a-rabbit-and-an-apple-a-child-eats-the-apple-and-plays.html): It's an appeal to nature: it suggests that what is right is what a child would do by instinct. Natural doesn't define right, and vegans point out this same mistake in "it's natural to eat meat". If children had the urge to bite the rabbit, that would not make it just to kill it.
- [V30. Humans are biologically herbivores.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/humans-are-biologically-herbivores.html): It isn't an ethical argument. It suggests we should be vegan because we can't make use of meat, milk and eggs, not because exploiting animals is wrong.
- [V31. It's proven that meat played no role in human evolution.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/its-proven-that-meat-played-no-role-in-human-evolution.html): It overstates a real study. Barr and colleagues showed in 2022 that the apparent increase in evidence of meat-eating in the time of *Homo erectus* disappears once research effort is accounted for. That weakens one hypothesis, but it doesn't prove meat played no role.
- [V32. Gorillas, bulls and horses get strong eating only plants.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/gorillas-bulls-and-horses-get-strong-eating-only-plants.html): It's a false analogy. Cattle digest grass with the help of microbes in the rumen, and horses ferment fiber in the large intestine; the microbes turn fiber and other compounds into nutrients, including protein. Gorillas spend much of the day eating large volumes of leaves and have a gut adapted to ferment them. The human digestive system doesn't work like that.
- [V33. Broccoli and spinach have more protein than meat.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/broccoli-and-spinach-have-more-protein-than-meat.html): The confusion comes from charts that count protein per calorie, not per weight. About half of spinach's calories come from protein, but it has very few calories: 100 g provides only about 3 g of protein.
- [V34. Vegans don't need to supplement B12.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/vegans-dont-need-to-supplement-b12.html): It is irresponsible and can put people's health at risk. Calling supplementation "a pharmaceutical industry scam" is a conspiracy claim with no evidence.
- [V35. All the B12 in meat comes from supplements.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/all-the-b12-in-meat-comes-from-supplements.html): It's an exaggeration. Farmed pigs and chickens get B12 in their feed, but in cattle B12 is produced by bacteria in the rumen from cobalt, which doesn't always need to be added.
- [V36. Anemia mostly affects meat eaters.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/anemia-mostly-affects-meat-eaters.html): It's a base-rate fallacy: since most people eat meat, most cases of almost anything occur among meat eaters. That doesn't show that meat causes anemia.
- [V37. Every nutrition body in the world approves vegan diets for everyone.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/every-nutrition-body-in-the-world-approves-vegan-diets-for-everyone.html): It overstates the consensus. The US Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics and the British Dietetic Association say well-planned vegan diets can be appropriate at every stage of life. But the German Nutrition Society, in 2024, neither recommended nor advised against vegan diets for pregnant women, children and older adults, for lack of data, and European pediatric bodies are cautious.
- [V38. Doctors don't know anything about nutrition.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/doctors-dont-know-anything-about-nutrition.html): It's a generalization. Nutrition training in medical school is often short, but that doesn't mean no doctor understands the subject, and many specialize in it.
- [V39. Unseasoned meat tastes of nothing; all the flavor comes from seasoning.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/unseasoned-meat-tastes-of-nothing-all-the-flavor-comes-from-seasoning.html): It's an exaggeration. Meat has its own flavor, which comes from fat, from compounds like heme iron and from the reactions that happen when it browns.
- [V40. Cats can't be vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/cats-cant-be-vegan.html): Many vegans repeat this as if it were established fact, but the available evidence points the other way.
