In a study of 1,369 cats published in PLOS ONE in 2023, the 127 fed a vegan diet tended to be as healthy or healthier on all seven general indicators, and a 2021 study of more than a thousand cats in Canada and the US also found no harm. A vegan cat food tested at the Federal University of Lavras, in Brazil, met the cats' needs on the measures assessed.
- [V41. Vegans are sexier and better in bed.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/vegans-are-sexier-and-better-in-bed.html): It takes the focus off the animals and appeals to the listener's self-interest.
- [V42. It's proven that vegans are more empathetic.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/its-proven-that-vegans-are-more-empathetic.html): The claim usually relies on a 2010 neuroimaging study of 60 people, which measured brain activation in response to images, not behavior. It is modest evidence, not proof.
- [V43. Koko the gorilla held conversations in sign language.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/koko-the-gorilla-held-conversations-in-sign-language.html): Koko learned many signs, but the claim that she used a language, with grammar and new sentences, does not hold up: the interpretation depended heavily on her trainers.
- [V44. Oysters and mussels feel pain like any other animal.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/oysters-and-mussels-feel-pain-like-any-other-animal.html): The evidence of sentience in bivalves is weak: they have very simple nervous systems with no centralized brain, and even animal advocates admit they may not feel.
- [V45. Livestock pollutes more than all cars, planes and ships combined.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/livestock-pollutes-more-than-all-cars-planes-and-ships-combined.html): The phrase comes from the 2006 FAO report, which compared livestock's 18% of emissions with about 13% for transport. But the accounting differed: for livestock it counted the whole chain, from feed to slaughter; for transport, only fuel combustion. One of the authors acknowledged the problem in 2010.
- [V46. Livestock causes 51% of the world's greenhouse gas emissions.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/livestock-causes-51-of-the-worlds-greenhouse-gas-emissions.html): The figure comes from a 2009 piece published by the Worldwatch Institute, which counted, for example, animal respiration, something international methodologies do not count as emissions. It became famous through the documentary *Cowspiracy*.
- [V47. Animal testing is useless: 90% of drugs fail.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/animal-testing-is-useless-90-of-drugs-fail.html): It's an exaggeration. About 90% of drug candidates fail in human trials, and species differences are one of the causes. But failures have many other causes, and the figure doesn't prove that tests have never helped.
- [V48. Science proves veganism is right.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/science-proves-veganism-is-right.html): Science answers questions of fact, such as whether animals feel pain and whether a vegan diet can be healthy. Whether it is right to cause that suffering is a moral question, which no study answers on its own.
- [V49. Food that may contain traces of milk isn't vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/food-that-may-contain-traces-of-milk-isnt-vegan.html): "May contain traces" is a warning for people with allergies: the product went through machines that also process that ingredient. The ingredient isn't in the recipe.
- [V50. Cultivated meat isn't vegan, because it comes from animals.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/cultivated-meat-isnt-vegan-because-it-comes-from-animals.html): The definitional objection confuses the letter of the commitment with its spirit: veganism is not a closed list of forbidden ingredients, it is a commitment to ending unnecessary harm to sentient beings.
- [V51. A good vegan only eats natural, organic, healthy food.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/a-good-vegan-only-eats-natural-organic-healthy-food.html): Nothing in vegan ethics requires that. The concern is not exploiting animals, whether dinner is an organic salad or French fries.
- [V52. Anyone who buys products from big companies isn't vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/anyone-who-buys-products-from-big-companies-isnt-vegan.html): Veganism is about the exploitation of animals. A vegan product from a big company involves no animal exploitation in the product itself. Criticisms of big companies can be legitimate, but they are a different discussion.
- [V53. Anyone who supports capitalism isn't really vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/anyone-who-supports-capitalism-isnt-really-vegan.html): It is the same mistake as demanding that vegans be anti-capitalist, in the opposite direction: it turns an economic position into a condition for defending animals.
- [V54. Anyone who supports step-by-step change isn't really vegan.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/anyone-who-supports-step-by-step-change-isnt-really-vegan.html): Veganism is defined by refusing animal exploitation as far as is possible and practicable, not by a position on strategy. Someone can be vegan and support gradual reforms, or be vegan and reject them.
- [V55. Anyone who won't accept gradual change doesn't understand how the world works.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/anyone-who-wont-accept-gradual-change-doesnt-understand-how-the-world.html): It mirrors the previous item, said by supporters of gradual change against those who call for an immediate end to exploitation. Asking people to stop now isn't naive: it states the goal clearly.
- [V56. Vegans should focus only on direct activism, talking to people one by one.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/vegans-should-focus-only-on-direct-activism-talking-to-people-one-by.html): Talking to each person matters: it changes habits, makes new vegans and creates people who later support laws and campaigns. But doing only that leaves aside what changes the lives of many animals at once.
- [V57. Vegans should focus only on institutional activism, changing laws, rules and court rulings.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/vegans-should-focus-only-on-institutional-activism-changing-laws.html): Changing laws, regulations and court rulings is what the available evidence supports most, and it is essential. But laws need public support to be passed and, above all, to last.
- [V58. Vegans should focus only on powerful and influential people.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/vegans-should-focus-only-on-powerful-and-influential-people.html): Influential people can change a lot at once, and some respond better to well-built arguments. But research on the question points to no consensus in favour of focusing on them.
- [V59. On a desert island, I'd starve before eating an animal.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/on-a-desert-island-id-starve-before-eating-an-animal.html): The very definition of veganism speaks of avoiding exploitation "as far as is possible and practicable". In a real survival situation, not eating an animal may be beyond what is possible, and saying otherwise creates a demand veganism does not make.
- [V60. I'm vegan, but I don't think everyone should be.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/im-vegan-but-i-dont-think-everyone-should-be.html): It treats as personal taste something that has a victim. No one says "I'm against assaulting people, but I don't think everyone should be." If the harm is unjust when you cause it, it is also unjust when someone else does.
- [V61. I'm vegan, but I have nothing against people who eat meat.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/im-vegan-but-i-have-nothing-against-people-who-eat-meat.html): It is a very common line, said to avoid conflict, and the intention is good: respecting people. But it mixes two things, having nothing against the person and having nothing against what they do.
- [V62. I'm vegan, but I taste the food when I visit my family.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/im-vegan-but-i-taste-the-food-when-i-visit-my-family.html): If the reason not to eat animals is the animal, it doesn't change because the table belongs to your family. For whoever died, the occasion makes no difference.
- [V63. My partner isn't vegan, but we accept our differences.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/my-partner-isnt-vegan-but-we-accept-our-differences.html): Respecting differences is important, and real relationships require care: no one has to break with someone they love over a disagreement, and there is no single formula. It is a controversial question.
- [V64. Veganism is only about animals; nothing else matters.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/veganism-is-only-about-animals-nothing-else-matters.html): Veganism does focus on animal exploitation, but that's no license to treat other humans unfairly or with prejudice. Humans are sentient too, and the criterion applies to them.
- [V65. Being vegan requires being anti-capitalist.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/being-vegan-requires-being-anti-capitalist.html): When someone says this without saying, just as firmly, that anti-capitalists should be vegan, the real goal isn't animal welfare. It's recruiting supporters for another cause from inside the vegan movement.
- [V66. Veganism and environmentalism without class struggle is just gardening.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/veganism-and-environmentalism-without-class-struggle-is-just-gardening.html): The phrase comes from a widely repeated saying, "ecology without class struggle is gardening", often attributed to the Brazilian activist Chico Mendes. Applied to veganism, it mixes two different causes: environmentalism does not presuppose veganism as a moral position. At most, for technical and evidential reasons, it recommends reducing animal farming because of its impact.
- [V67. More expensive meat is bad for ordinary people.](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/stop-saying/more-expensive-meat-is-bad-for-ordinary-people.html): When the price of animal products rises, the drop in consumption is usually treated only as sad news, and not also as what it is: fewer animals killed.

## Political and ethical objections

- [Liberalism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/liberalism.html): Freedom is a right of rational individuals; animals aren't subjects of liberal rights. Protect individuals against harm caused by others and ensure each can live their own life. For the English philosopher John Stuart Mill (1806–1873), one of the leading names of liberalism, the only legitimate reason to limit someone's freedom is to prevent harm to others. This is the harm principle, which he sets out in On Liberty (1859).
- [Libertarianism and anarcho-capitalism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/libertarianism.html): What's mine is mine: animals are property, and the freedom to use property is sacred. Self-ownership and the non-aggression principle: no one may initiate violence against another individual.
- [Conservatism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/conservatism.html): Eating meat is tradition, and conservatives preserve what has worked; animal rights are a modern invention. Preserve the institutions, customs and bonds that have proved valuable over time, change with prudence and cultivate duties toward those who depend on us.
- [Marxism, socialism and communism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/marxism.html): Exploitation is a relation between human classes. Animals aren't workers, and the struggle is a different one. End exploitation and the turning of beings and lives into commodities.
- [Anarchism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/anarchism.html): Anarchism fights domination between people; animals are not part of that. Reject hierarchies and forms of domination that cannot be justified.
- [Utilitarianism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/utilitarianism.html): Human pleasures are worth more: better to be a human dissatisfied than a pig satisfied. Maximize well-being and minimize suffering for everyone affected, counting each one's interest equally.
- [Contractualism and Rawlsian justice](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/contractualism.html): Justice holds among those who have a sense of justice and can make agreements. Choose the rules of a society impartially, as if we did not know what position we would occupy in it.
- [Deontology and Kantianism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/deontology.html): Only rational beings are ends in themselves; toward animals we have, at most, indirect duties. Treat beings who have value of their own as ends, and never merely as means.
- [Communitarianism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/communitarianism.html): Duties arise from the community and its traditions, and animals are not members of it. Morality is built in the bonds and practices of a community.
- [Egalitarianism and prioritarianism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/egalitarianism.html): Equality is among human citizens; animals belong to another category. Reduce unjust inequalities and give priority to those who are worst off.
- [Ethics of care](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/care-ethics.html): Care applies to close relationships, not to unknown animals. Respond to the needs of the vulnerable and the dependent with attention and responsibility.
- [Virtue ethics](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/virtue-ethics.html): Virtue is about human character; treating animals well matters only because it makes us better. Cultivate virtues like compassion, justice and temperance, and avoid vices like cruelty.
- [Feminism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/feminism.html): Feminism is about women; talking about cows and hens is changing the subject, or even offensive. End oppression linked to sex and control over the body and reproduction.
- [Anti-racism and anti-ableism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/anti-discrimination.html): Comparing speciesism to racism or ableism is offensive; they are different things. Do not give less weight to someone's interests because of a trait that does not change how much they can be harmed, such as race, disability, origin or appearance.
- [The progressive left and multiculturalism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/progressive-left-and-multiculturalism.html): The animal cause is a white middle-class concern that ends up attacking the cultural practices of minorities. Defend vulnerable groups, fight domination and respect cultural diversity.
- [Pacifism and nonviolence](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/pacifism.html): Nonviolence is a commitment between people, not to animals. Refuse violence as a means of resolving conflicts and reaching goals.
- [Effective altruism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/effective-altruism.html): Resources for doing good are limited, and should go to humans first. Use evidence and reason to do the most good possible with the resources available.
- [Environmentalism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/environmentalism.html): What matters is saving the planet, ecosystems and species, not each individual animal. Protect the environment and the planet: conserve ecosystems, biodiversity and natural resources, and secure living conditions for present and future generations.
- [Pragmatism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/pragmatism.html): Politics is the art of the possible: the animal cause is not viable, wins no votes, and there are more practical problems to solve. Judge ideas and policies by their practical consequences, not by loyalty to a doctrine; test, look at the results and correct course.
- [Stoicism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/stoicism.html): Animals lack reason, so there is no justice between us and them; the Stoic tends to their own virtue. Virtue is the only good: live in accordance with reason and nature, with justice, courage, temperance and wisdom, and accept what does not depend on us.
- [Natural law and Thomism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/natural-law.html): In the natural order, animals exist for human use; killing them for food is legitimate. Do good and avoid evil, knowing through reason the basic goods of human nature, such as life, knowledge and community, and never attacking them directly.
- [Religious ethics and divine command](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/religious-ethics.html): God gave humans dominion over animals; if He allowed it, there is nothing wrong with eating them. What is right is what God commands, or what agrees with God's good nature, known through scripture and tradition.
- [Discourse ethics](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/discourse-ethics.html): A moral norm is valid if everyone accepts it in rational dialogue; animals cannot take part in dialogue, so they are left out. A norm is valid only if everyone affected by it could accept it in a free dialogue, in which only the force of the better argument counts. This is the proposal of the German philosophers Jürgen Habermas and Karl-Otto Apel.
- [Ethical egoism and Objectivism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/egoism-objectivism.html): Everyone should pursue their own interest; I owe nothing to animals if I gain nothing from it. Each person should act in their own rational interest. In Ayn Rand's Objectivism, one's own life is the standard of value, and rights protect the freedom of action of rational beings.
- [Moral relativism and subjectivism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/relativism.html): Morality is relative: each culture and each person decides what is right, and no one can say that eating meat is wrong. There are no universal moral truths: right and wrong depend on culture (cultural relativism), on each person's attitudes (subjectivism) or on emotions and preferences (emotivism).
- [Humanism and anthropocentrism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/political/humanism.html): I'm a humanist: human dignity comes first, and putting animals on the same level demeans humans. Value human dignity, reason and well-being, and base ethics on reason, empathy and evidence, not on dogma.

## Beyond veganism

- [Antispeciesism and sentientism](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/antispeciesism.html): Veganism is one consequence of a broader criterion: what matters morally is the capacity to be harmed or benefited.
- [The state of the art in animal ethics](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/state-of-the-art.html): Since 1975, animal ethics has been tested on ever harder cases, by authors from schools that disagree with each other, and has reached the same rejection of speciesism.
- [Wild animal suffering](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/wild-animals.html): Hunger, disease and predation were not caused by us. But if sentience is what matters, this suffering cannot be dismissed just because it is natural.
- [Sentience in AI and robots](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/ai-and-robots.html): No current system is recognized as sentient. But the possibility is not absurd, and the criterion does not depend on what a being is made of.
- [The definition of veganism, debated](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/defining-veganism.html): What defines veganism: refusing the exploitation of animals, or refusing everything of animal origin? The question has come back strongly with cultivated meat and precision fermentation.
- [Sentience in extraterrestrials, plants and other forms of life](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/extraterrestrials.html): There is no evidence of life beyond Earth, let alone sentient life, and no robust evidence that plants or fungi feel. Both questions test whether our criterion is really a criterion, and what we would do if the evidence changed.
- [What supports animal ethics, and what weakens it](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/foundations.html): Critical reason, relevance, impartiality and sentience support veganism and animal ethics. Partiality, relativism, tribalism, ableism, making abstractions sacred and weak will weaken them.
- [Restraint with indirect arguments](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/direct-arguments.html): Just as vegans should be careful when criticizing other vegans, those who use health and environment arguments should be careful not to strengthen anthropocentrism and environmentalism, which work against animals.
- [The common minimum](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/common-minimum.html): Finding the point of convergence: someone who rejects the whole conclusion can almost always accept part of it. Showing that part is not giving up what you argue for, it is not demanding that people change their worldview before taking the first step.
- [When logic isn't enough](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/when-logic-isnt-enough.html): Facts and arguments show what is right, but they rarely suffice to make someone change. Apathy, habit and indifference call for other reasons: someone to care about, people to change with and an easy path to follow.
- [The currents of the vegan movement](https://fortheanimals.biblioverse.org/beyond/currents-of-veganism.html): All vegans want the end of animal exploitation. The currents disagree about why, with whom and how to get there. A map of the ends, the means and the main debates.
